text:
angela: heads up — we're seeing a ~3x increase in 5xx (mostly 503) from hosted inference starting ~20m after the canary rolled. customer-reported latency/timeouts are spiking too. I can see the canary rollout id 2026-09-04T10:02 in deploy dashboard.

alert-bot: [ALERT] inference.gateway: 503 rate > 300 rpm for service=hosted-inference (10m)

support-ops: multiple paying customers are getting errors in prod. one support ticket includes a curl repro and stack traces. escalating to SRE/Runtime.

jonathan: looking now. first glance: gateway logs show 502/503 upstream resets when requests hit model-proxy group rp-inference-3.

maria: the canary applied a new feature flag flip: `enable_kv_cache_v2=true` + a batching tweak `batch_max_latency_ms=20`. both set as canary.

jonathan: that matches. I'm seeing increased socket timeouts between gateway and model-proxy on nodes that picked the canary. non-canary nodes are fine.

angela: do we have an automated rollback policy for that rollout?

deploy-bot: rollout 2026-09-04T10:02 status: canary 30% -> 100% in progress. no automated rollback triggered.

maria: I pushed the flag change earlier to test perf for short-context workloads. might be regressing connection handling under high concurrency.

jonathan: quick mitigation: revert the flag on canary slice or pause rollout to prevent further traffic. I'm going to scale down canary weight to 0 for now unless someone objects.

angela: do it. also notify DS/customers that we got a mitigation underway. support-ops can you draft a short blurb?

support-ops: yes — drafting now. will include repro curl and ask customers to retry after ~10m.

jonathan: executing rollback command: `redwoodctl rollout update --id 2026-09-04T10:02 --canary-weight 0`

infra-bot: action accepted. rollout update queued. expected propagation ~30s.

jonathan: propagation shows canary traffic -> 0. observing error rate dropping on gateway for the nodes we changed.

angela: good. what's the root cause hypothesis so we can follow up?

maria: initial hypothesis: `enable_kv_cache_v2` interacts poorly with the new batching path under high open connections — KV cache warming is causing long latent disk access or synchronous RPCs to redis layer, leading to connection stalls and gateway timeouts.

jonathan: corroborating: model-proxy logs include repeated `ERR: kv_fetch_timeout` and the gateway stack shows `upstream read: connection reset by peer` around the same timestamps.

support-ops: customer repro (from ticket):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/fast-1","input":"short prompt"}'
```
response: `503 Service Unavailable` (most attempts) or long hang then 502.

angela: OK. action items: 1) keep rollback in place 2) run canary-only smoke tests with `enable_kv_cache_v2=false` to confirm baseline 3) runtime team to instrument KV calls and add timeouts/retries 4) postmortem + customer comms. anyone add to that list?

maria: also we'll add guardrails to the canary config: don't enable `enable_kv_cache_v2` without staged kernel config and longer canary dwell for 5xx signal.

jonathan: I'll follow up with a quick runbook update: if a canary increases 5xx by >50% within 30m, auto-pause and roll back.

support-ops: sent customers a holding message: "We've temporarily rolled back a recent change that affected hosted inference. We're monitoring and will update in 30 minutes."

angela: logging this incident now. tagging oncall. please paste any relevant logs in this thread for the postmortem.

maria: attaching model-proxy excerpt (snips):
```
[2026-09-04T10:18:02Z] ERR kv_fetch_timeout key=ctx_abc123 duration_ms=10234
[2026-09-04T10:18:02Z] WARN connection pool exhausted
[2026-09-04T10:18:03Z] ERR upstream read: connection reset by peer
```

jonathan: gateway excerpt:
```
[2026-09-04T10:18:05Z] 503 "GET /v1/generate" host=api... upstream=rp-inference-3/10.0.5.12:8080 "upstream read: connection reset by peer"
[2026-09-04T10:18:06Z] 502 "POST /v1/chat" host=api... upstream=rp-inference-3/10.0.5.12:8080 "no healthy upstream"
```

angela: great. let's meet in 10 to triage root cause and timeline for a safe re-roll with additional telemetry + throttles.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-09-04-94. severity: high. assigned: jonathan, maria, angela.

support-ops: will keep ticket owners updated and escalate further if we see customer impact after rollback window.

jonathan: monitoring dashboards show 5xx rate returning to baseline after canary weight -> 0. I'll keep this thread updated if anything regresses.

angela: thanks all — good containment. we'll run a formal postmortem and add a canary-safety checklist."
